featured_reviews.name: Jatin Solanki
featured_reviews.review_text:
They gave property on rent higher than market rate. Despite paying 12 months' rent in advance and commission well before time, they did not provide flat on time. When I called Advocate Chavan and told to return my full rent as I didn't get flat on time, she told me to pay one month rent to cancel agreement. I must say all 5 stars given here are fake. Don't trust this fake rating. Don't contact this agent. You will suffer a lot.

To answer your reply: when I approached for the property shown on portal, they told me property is not available now and offered me other property. For delay, it was agreed well before 2 weeks when full payment was done to give property on said date. But you and landlord took it very lightly to give possession on time. When we raised our concern and asked to give our rent back then only you and landlord came to action and vacated property. Why should we pay one month rent when we had not got property on time mentioned in agreement?
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
We would like to clarify the concerns raised in this review.

Mr. Solanki approached us through our online advertisement, where all rental details were clearly mentioned, including the market-aligned pricing. After full understanding and agreement, he proceeded to sign and legally register the rental agreement.

As per standard legal terms, a one-month notice period is mandatory for cancellation after registration. We, as mediators, are required to follow these rules as agreed upon by both parties.

Regarding the possession delay, there was a minor and unavoidable delay of one day due to the previous tenant vacating slightly later than planned. The same was communicated in advance, and we ensured proper coordination so that Mr. Solanki could move into the flat without further issues.

We always strive to maintain transparency and professionalism in our dealings. We request everyone to consider complete facts before forming an opinion.

featured_reviews.name: Sakib Mulla
featured_reviews.review_text:
Nestled amidst the lush landscapes of Srisailam Highway, Primal Aranya is less of a residential development and more of an ecological statement. It represents a sophisticated departure from the sterile, concrete-heavy luxury often found in modern urban sprawl, pivoting instead toward a "forest-first" philosophy that seamlessly integrates high-end living with the raw tranquility of nature.
The architectural intent here is clearly biophilic, emphasizing expansive open spaces, natural ventilation, and a layout that honors the existing topography. What distinguishes Aranya is its commitment to "Quiet Luxury"—it avoids the ostentatious in favor of organic textures, curated greenery, and an infrastructure that promotes wellness. The amenities are thoughtfully decentralized, ensuring that whether you are at the clubhouse or on a jogging trail, the boundary between the built environment and the wilderness remains beautifully blurred.
From an investment perspective, its strategic location near the Pharma City and the ORR ensures robust appreciation, yet the project feels worlds away from the industrial hum. It caters perfectly to the discerning homeowner who seeks a sanctuary that doesn’t compromise on connectivity. Primal Aranya isn't just offering a plot or a villa; it is offering a rhythmic way of life governed by the seasons rather than the clock. For those looking to escape the hyper-compressed lifestyle of central Hyderabad without sacrificing modern comforts, Aranya stands as a premier benchmark in sustainable luxury.

featured_reviews.name: Patrick Stars
featured_reviews.review_text:
I strongly advise not buying a flat in Monte South. The experience here has been nothing short of disappointing and frustrating. The environment is not what we expected from a so-called “luxury” residence. Instead of a peaceful and upscale living experience, we are facing constant issues that make daily life difficult.

The biggest issue is the kind of people living here—many lack basic manners, and the atmosphere feels unrefined. There’s a lot of unnecessary show-off, but no real sense of community or decency. Some residents engage in unacceptable behavior, like spitting from upper floors, which is absolutely disgusting. The construction noise is unbearable, and the entire project seems poorly managed.

The staff is extremely rude and unprofessional. It’s clear that cheap labor has been hired, and there is no training in basic courtesy or service. The maintenance is a complete scam—overpriced, yet the facilities are in terrible condition. The air conditioning doesn’t even work in the lifts, making it suffocating to go up to higher floors. Hygiene is another huge issue—garbage and mosquitoes are everywhere, and pan stains cover the parking areas.

One of the most frustrating and recurring problems is the water supply. Every week, there is some issue—pipes breaking, dirty water flowing, or no water at all. Imagine being in the middle of a shower, cooking, or hosting guests, and suddenly there’s no water for hours! Right now, in my house, there has been no water in the kitchen for two days, except for one washroom. Despite multiple complaints, nothing has been resolved. The plumber comes and does nothing, and management responds with a casual “K” after several emails. It’s unacceptable.

We moved here expecting a high-quality lifestyle with minimal distress, but instead, it has been the complete opposite. This place is exhausting and mentally draining. People seem indifferent to the problems around them, and there is no accountability. The entire experience has made me realize the value of my old home, where life was peaceful, the energy was positive, and basic necessities like clean water were never a problem.

At this point, I am seriously considering leaving because the situation here is beyond frustrating. I regret moving here and would not recommend it to anyone looking for a genuinely comfortable and luxurious living experience. Not a homely feeling here.
There was even a fire here.
Video below shows how many insects and mosquitos come everyday.

featured_reviews.name: Amey Manchekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
New Hind Mill MHADA Sankul strikes a balance between affordable housing and urban convenience. The flats are modest — 1BHK with basic amenities, compact size (≈225 sq ft carpet area) but nicely built, with lifts, good flooring, fixed kitchen platforms and reliable structure.

The neighbourhood is vibrant — shopping, local markets, plenty of small eateries & transport links are easily accessible, which is a big plus. However, parking is tight, noise & congestion are noticeable, especially during peak hours.

All in all, if you’re okay with smaller spaces and don’t mind urban hustle, it offers great value for the location.
